title: api-robustness-standardize-rate-limits-idempotency-retry-after-streaming-openai-compat
author: Priya Kapoor
commits: feat(api): add Retry-After mapping and standard rate-limit headers to OpenAI compat layer
fix(idempotency): implement cross-region idempotency store and dedupe logic for completions
chore(tests): add integration tests for idempotency replays and Retry-After behavior
fix(streaming): ensure graceful stream termination with OpenAI-style error events on mid-stream rate limits
docs: update API docs and compat notes for idempotency and rate-limit semantics
description:
Motivation: Customers and SDKs expect consistent rate-limit semantics and idempotency behavior across Redwood's native API and the OpenAI-compatibility layer. Streaming endpoints, function/tool-calling flows, and structured outputs currently have a few inconsistent error formats and header shapes which cause SDKs to implement brittle heuristics. This PR standardizes rate-limit headers (RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset), adds a deterministic Retry-After header mapping, and aligns error payloads with OpenAI compatibility expectations (error.{message,type,param,code}).

What this change does:
- OpenAI compat layer: map internal rate-limit and resource errors to OpenAI-style error JSON and include Retry-After in seconds when applicable. Ensures 429/503 mapping is consistent.
- Headers: emit RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch seconds) for both native and compat endpoints. Retry-After is present and authoritative when the service requests a client wait.
- Idempotency: implement a cross-region idempotency store for completion and non-streaming responses. If a request includes Idempotency-Key, we now: (a) dedupe identical requests to avoid double-execution/billing, (b) return the stored response for repeated keys, (c) TTL is configurable (default 24h). For function/tool-calls we record invocation results and return cached outputs; side-effecting tools are marked best-effort and documented.
- Streaming stability: disallow server-side idempotency for true streaming responses (server-sent events/HTTP chunking) because partial streams cannot be safely deduped; instead we: (a) reject requests with Idempotency-Key that use streaming=true with 400 and clear guidance in the error.message, (b) add a graceful mid-stream error event type 'error' with OpenAI-compatible error object when a rate-limit or backend failure occurs mid-stream so SDKs can surface a consistent event.
- Function/tool-calling and structured output: ensure function-calling invocations report an invocation_id and are included in idempotency cache keys. Structured output validators updated to avoid transient 422s when recoverable auxiliary checks fail; map to 409/400 consistently where appropriate.
- Observability: add metrics and tracing spans for: idempotency.cache.hit, idempotency.cache.write, rate_limit.enforced, rate_limit.exceeded_midstream.

Testing and validation:
- Unit: mapping tests for error payloads and headers.
- Integration: end-to-end test that replays identical requests with same Idempotency-Key and asserts single backend invocation and identical response body.
- E2E: streaming failure injection test that simulates a mid-stream 429 and verifies the client receives a final 'error' event formatted to OpenAI compat.

Backward compatibility: Where possible we preserve existing headers for native endpoints. The compat layer adapts internal errors to the expected OpenAI shape; this is additive and should not break SDKs that already handle the compat format. Idempotency behavior is only active when the client supplies Idempotency-Key. Streaming + Idempotency combinations now explicitly error to avoid silent data duplication.

Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag 'api.idempotency.enabled' (enabled for 25% of traffic initially), observability dashboards added to monitor idempotency cache hit ratio and rate-limit false positives. Linear tickets: ENG-4923 tracks rollout, PM-321 tracks docs/announcements.
review_conversation:
Alex Chen: Can we guarantee cross-region consistency for the idempotency store?
Priya Kapoor: We use the existing global CDC-backed cache with linearizable writes for the small namespace we use; documented TTLs and fallbacks in handler. Added tests to simulate cross-region failover.
Morgan Lee: Streaming mid-stream errors may break some older SDKs that expect only stop events.
Priya Kapoor: Agreed — we added clear docs and an explicit compat note, and the mid-stream event uses the same 'error' event shape OpenAI clients already handle. Also added a feature flag to limit rollout.
Sofia Alvarez: Please ensure telemetry includes a label that indicates whether a response was served from idempotency cache.
Priya Kapoor: Added idempotency.cache.* metrics and included the cache_source tag in traces.
Alex Chen: CI showed a flakey streaming test on first run, then passed after rerun; please keep an eye on that test in canary.
Priya Kapoor: Noted; added extra retries and a deterministic backoff in the test harness.
ci_details: CI run 1: build passed, unit tests passed, integration streaming_test flakey->fail. CI run 2 (rerun): all checks passed. Checks: lint: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e: pass, security-scan: pass.
release_notes:
- Standardize rate-limit headers and Retry-After semantics across native and OpenAI compat endpoints.
- Add Idempotency-Key deduplication for non-streaming completions and function/tool-call caching (default TTL 24h).
- Streaming: explicit rejection of streaming requests with Idempotency-Key; graceful mid-stream 'error' events with OpenAI-compatible payloads.
- Observability: new idempotency and rate-limit metrics.
